Well, everyone is entitled to their own opinion and I am glad you shared yours. When I said roughly five hours I didn't mean five hours exactly. I meant that picking up on the blatant contextual clues and only conversing with Delilah when the player needs it along with completing required objectives, of course. Not everyone's first playthrough is going to be the same, but that was the length of my first run. As I wrote in the review, I played through it thrice.

I did not have issues with the lack of a GPS, but I grew up before such devices were available to the consumer market. The inclusion of a GPS would have broke the time frame aspect of the game's setting. It takes place in the mid 1980s. I actually did some research into this and GPS devices existed, but not for the civilian sector. It was a technology that had been exclusive to the military through the entire decade, so it would not have made sense for Henry to have such a device.
